about: Tested versions of the Mizzey stack. Evidence for these versions only, not a production compatibility guarantee. Change only through the regression path in docs/stack-and-upgrades.md. corex.lock remains the file tools/corex-sync.mjs reads; the corex entry here must match it (checked by tools/repo_checks.py). For most components version is the exact tested version. For wordpress it is the compatibility pin, because the checker compares it with corex.lock, and the exact tested runtime is in observed_runtime: see the governance-model limitation in docs/stack-and-upgrades.md.
verified_in: local disposable runtime ../app/wp built by tools/corex-sync.mjs (WAMP, Windows)

database.notes: Every discovery probe and every product-cost integration scenario ran against this engine. The production engine is set with hosting (OD-27)

wordpress.source: compatibility_pin from corex.lock, which tools/corex-sync.mjs installs from; observed_runtime read from wp-includes/version.php and get_bloginfo('version') in ../app/wp on 2026-10-29
wordpress.notes: WordPress applied its own patch updates within the pinned 7.1 line, to 7.1.4. On 2026-10-29 the integration suite (25 scenarios, 0 failed), probes P-006, P-012, P-016, P-017, P-019 and P-020, and the bilingual product, cart, checkout and email checks ran against 7.1.4 with CoreX v0.47.0 (PR #351). release_pack.py fetches observed_runtime, so the release now carries 7.1.4. The version field has to equal corex.lock's entry (tools/repo_checks.py), so for this one component it carries the compatibility pin rather than the exact tested runtime, which observed_runtime records instead (D-20 row D7 separates them in the checker)

woocommerce.source: plugin header; discovery probes P-001 to P-021 ran against it
woocommerce.notes: HPOS and Cost of Goods Sold behaviour recorded against this version (P-016, P-017)

corex.notes: Tested 2026-10-29 on the disposable runtime ../app/wp (WordPress 7.1.4, WooCommerce 11.1.0, WPML 4.9.7, WCML 5.5.7, PHP 8.3.6, MySQL 8.3.0): database snapshot first; vendor tree installed from v0.47.0's composer.lock; schema 3 to 4 applied on the first WP-CLI load (a dry run as the first command reports would-migrate and the load still applies it), wp corex migrate then already-current; restored from the pre-upgrade dump under v0.47.0 and migrated again; options compared before and after; corex#201 reproduction passes on a --no-dev install; integration suite 25 scenarios, 0 failed; probes P-012, P-016, P-017, P-019 unchanged, P-006 and P-020 changed and reproduced the same with v0.42.0 code, so not isolated to this upgrade; file revert to v0.42.0 on schema 4 serves the site; English and Arabic product, cart and checkout with an item, no script error; WooCommerce order emails (English, Arabic right to left) and one CoreX email captured at pre_wp_mail, one call each, not delivered; HPOS compatible list clean; build-dist and a trial pack built. Release packaging with WordPress 7.1.4 verified in PR #418 using the unmodified built tree. Server staging verification on MariaDB 11.4 remains pending

paymob.notes: PAY-13 contracts Paymob's official WooCommerce integration (specs/028-payments). Its callback, signature and refund code was read for the payment layer, which verifies every callback before the plugin acts. t68-payments covers the layer in process and, over HTTP to the local runtime (WordPress 7.1.4, WooCommerce 11.1.0, 1 November 2026), signed and forged callbacks and refunds through this plugin version, with Paymob's API reply stood in for. The Paymob sandbox run on staging with Paymob's own callbacks is still to come (specs/028-payments T010). The release packer bundles it in its own tooling pull request
